findings.F1: The main measure is on the side the idea predicts but far too small to show here: +0.33 % unusual 5-day fall per case (t 0.49, 422 cases on 244 days), a strength of 0.025 of the coin's usual 10.60 % move. The coin's normal drift against the short (-0.65 %) leaves the total move at -0.32 %, which is -1.6 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: The effect flips sign by period. On the 5-day grid in the profile in folds B and C (93 cases), the unusual 5-day give-back is +6.05 % (t 2.94) in 2018, +2.40 % (t 2.05) in 2019 and +2.44 % (t 1.37) in 2021, but -3.19 % (t -2.46) in 2020. By window, w14 gives +6.78 % (t 3.38) and w16 gives -3.68 % (t -2.74). The market's own moves in each period drown a small average.
findings.F3: The grading the idea claims is not there. Step 5's share-given-back check, top minus bottom half of the forecast, has a Welch t of -1.87, on the wrong side. In my 5-day quartiles of the scaled rise, q4 gives +1.11 % (t 0.51) against +3.98 % (t 2.84) for q2, with a Spearman correlation of only 0.08 between rise size and the 5-day give-back.
findings.F4: Where any give-back shows, it is quick and not graded at the top. On a 1-day grid (437 cases, the smallest independent samples) the 1-day give-back is +0.40 % (t 1.51), carried by the third quartile (+1.43 %, t 3.06), while the largest rises (q4) give back -0.19 % (t -0.30). The 2-day grid shows the same: q3 +2.02 % (t 2.85), q4 -0.60 %.
findings.F5: No single coin carries the effect. On the 5-day grid only ZEC passes t 2 (+4.84 %, t 2.03, 16 cases), while XMR is -0.56 % and the others sit between +0.21 % and +1.41 % with t under 0.8. More cases are available from the 13 other coins, which have data in folds A and D and in part of B and C.

ideas.name: rally giveback, all coins
ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's 3-day rise is against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the fall in its price over the next 5 days, taking back a larger share of that rise.
ideas.consequence: Multi-day rises in falling, agitated markets are mostly forced short covering, so they are partly given back once covering ends, more so the larger the rise against the coin's usual swing.
